clusters.name: Variables
clusters.fact: Variables are symbols that stand in for unknown or changing quantities.

unknown.text: The letter or symbol standing for the value an equation is solved to find.

term.text: A single piece of an algebraic expression, like 3x or 7 — one part of what's added or subtracted together.

expression.text: A combination of numbers, variables, and operations — unlike an equation, it has no equals sign.

clusters.name: Equations
clusters.fact: Equations state that two expressions are equal, and stay balanced under the same operation on both sides.

balance.text: The idea that both sides of an equation must stay equal — whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other.

solution.text: The value (or values) that make an equation true when substituted in.

clusters.name: Functions
clusters.fact: Functions map every input to exactly one output, describing how one quantity depends on another.

input.text: The value fed into a function — the independent variable, which the output then depends on.

output.text: The value a function produces from a given input — the dependent variable, since it depends on what's fed in.

domain.text: The full set of inputs a function is allowed to take.

range.text: The full set of outputs a function can produce, pairing with domain (its set of allowed inputs).

bridges.fact: Solving for x bridges the two: it's the act of isolating a variable by keeping an equation balanced.

info.text: The general process of isolating an unknown by applying the same operation to both sides of an equation.

bridges.fact: A graph bridges the two: it's the visual picture of both an equation's solutions and a function's input-output pairs.

info.text: The visual plot of a function's input-output pairs on a coordinate plane.
